dossiers.label: Callicles: the law of nature
dossiers.about: Callicles' challenge: convention is made by the weak many to tame the strong, but nature shows that the better should have more; a man of real nature would trample our spells and charms and rise up as master. And philosophy, fine for a boy, makes a grown man ridiculous.

passage.start_quote: ὦ Σώκρατες, δοκεῖς νεανιεύεσθαι ἐν τοῖς λόγοις

parts.label: According to the law of nature
parts.quote: κατὰ νόμον γε τὸν τῆς φύσεως

parts.label: We mould the best, like lion cubs, with spells
parts.quote: ὥσπερ λέοντας, κατεπᾴδοντές τε καὶ γοητεύοντες καταδουλούμεθα

parts.label: The slave rises up as our master
parts.quote: ἐπαναστὰς ἀνεφάνη δεσπότης ἡμέτερος ὁ δοῦλος

echoes.why: Thrasymachus in the Republic: justice is the advantage of the stronger.
Glaucon's restatement: by nature every creature pursues getting more.

related.why: Glaucon revives the case for nature over convention, with the ring.
Socrates answers Callicles' life of desire with the leaky jars.

dossiers.label: The leaky jars
dossiers.about: A wise man said the body is our tomb, and the desiring part of the soul a leaky jar; the uninitiated in Hades carry water to it in a sieve. Two men with jars: one sound and full, at rest; the other holed, filling day and night. Callicles prefers the second, and Socrates offers him the plover.

passage.start_quote: τὸ μὲν σῶμά ἐστιν ἡμῖν σῆμα

parts.label: The body is our tomb
parts.quote: τὸ μὲν σῶμά ἐστιν ἡμῖν σῆμα

parts.label: Desire, like a jar full of holes
parts.quote: ὡς τετρημένος εἴη πίθος, διὰ τὴν ἀπληστίαν ἀπεικάσας

parts.label: Which life is happier, the orderly or the intemperate?
parts.quote: λέγεις τὸν τοῦ ἀκολάστου εὐδαιμονέστερον εἶναι ἢ τὸν τοῦ κοσμίου

echoes.why: The Phaedrus: the soul imprisoned in the body like an oyster in its shell.
The Cratylus discusses the same derivation of σῶμα from σῆμα.

related.why: The Republic's image of insatiable appetite.

dossiers.label: The judgment of naked souls
dossiers.about: 'Hear a very fine account, which you will think a myth but I think true.' Under Cronus men were judged clothed and alive, by living judges, and judged wrongly; Zeus decreed that they be judged naked, dead, soul viewing soul, by Minos, Rhadamanthys and Aeacus.

passage.start_quote: ἄκουε δή, φασί, μάλα καλοῦ λόγου

parts.label: You will think it a myth, I think it true
parts.quote: ὃν σὺ μὲν ἡγήσῃ μῦθον, ὡς ἐγὼ οἶμαι, ἐγὼ δὲ λόγον

parts.label: Judged naked, soul looking at soul
parts.quote: αὐτῇ τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτὴν τὴν ψυχὴν θεωροῦντα

parts.label: Death the separation of soul and body
parts.quote: δυοῖν πραγμάτοιν διάλυσις, τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ τοῦ σώματος

parts.label: Let us follow this account as our guide
parts.quote: ὥσπερ οὖν ἡγεμόνι τῷ λόγῳ χρησώμεθα τῷ νῦν παραφανέντι
